help.title: Help
help.footer: Press ? or F1 to open this help anywhere.

icons.relationsIntro: Each end of a line says how many rows of THAT table can match one row of the table on the other end.

kind.1:1: One-to-one: one row on each side
kind.1:N: One-to-many: one row here, many there
kind.N:1: Many-to-one: many orders belong to one user (the usual foreign key)

icons.readHow: The foreign key lives on the “many” end. Drag from the dot at the edge of a column row to a column of another table to connect them; double-click a line to edit it.

col.key: Primary key (a composite key marks several columns)
col.fk: Foreign key: this column points to another table
col.unique: Unique: no two rows share this value
col.default: Has a default value (hover to read it)
col.index: Part of an index (hover to see which)
col.comment: Has a note (hover to read it)
col.nullable: A “?” after the type means the column may be empty (NULL)

ctl.insert: Insert a column above or below this row
ctl.linkDot: Drag from this dot onto a column to draw a relationship

tool.section: Section: a frame that groups tables
tool.note: Sticky note anywhere on the board

icons.kindsNote: These samples show the strict form (a row is always required). The editor also offers the optional forms: a circle means “zero”, so a line from “zero or many” to “exactly one” is a normal optional foreign key.

about.intro: ERD Editor draws database diagrams on an infinite canvas. You describe tables, columns, keys and relationships once; the program draws them, checks them and turns them into SQL, DBML, images and a briefing for an AI agent.
about.file: Everything lives in one .erd.json file next to your project: it is the only source of truth. SQL, DBML, PNG and SVG are generated from it and never edited by hand.

tables.title: Tables
tables.text: Double-click the canvas (or press T) to add a table. Drag to move; a table grows with its longest name.

columns.title: Columns
columns.text: Type a name and press Tab for the next column. Reorder with the drag handle or Alt+↑/↓; select several rows to move or delete them together.

types.title: Column types
types.text: Pick a type from the list and fill its parameters (length, precision, scale, enum values). Types that your database does not have are hidden; anything unusual stays editable as plain text.

relations.title: Relationships
relations.text: Drag from a column's dot to another table. Set both cardinalities, ON DELETE / ON UPDATE and a label; parallel lines are separated automatically.

indexes.title: Indexes
indexes.text: Select several columns and press Ctrl+I for a composite index. Choose the column order, unique and the index type.

sections.title: Sections
sections.text: A section is a frame that groups tables by area. A table belongs to it only while it lies completely inside; moving a section moves everything inside.

notes.title: Notes
notes.text: Every table, column and section can carry a note, and sticky notes can sit anywhere with their own color. Notes travel into the exports.

inspector.title: Inspector
inspector.text: The side panel edits whatever is selected: table, columns, relationships, section or sticky note. Toggle it with Ctrl+\.

search.title: Search
search.text: Ctrl+K finds tables, columns, sections, lines and notes by name, type or text, and jumps to the result.

tabs.title: Tabs and undo
tabs.text: Open several boards in tabs like an editor. Undo and redo cover everything, including moves and resizes.

file.title: One file
file.text: Open with from your file manager, or open and save from inside. Saving is atomic: a crash never leaves half a file.

exportSql.title: Export SQL
exportSql.text: CREATE TABLE, indexes and foreign keys for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server or plain ANSI. What a database cannot express is reported, not dropped silently.

exportDbml.title: Export DBML
exportDbml.text: Text for dbdiagram.io and other DBML tools, including colors, sections and notes.

exportImage.title: Export image
exportImage.text: PNG or SVG of the whole board, or only of the tables and sections you selected, in dark or light.

exportAgent.title: For an AI agent
exportAgent.text: A Markdown briefing: a short how-to-read guide, every table with its notes, relationships and a list of open points.

importSql.title: Import SQL
importSql.text: Paste or choose a schema dump (mysqldump, pg_dump, SQLite, SQL Server). It opens as a new board and tables are laid out near their relatives.

tip.alt: Select a column row, then [[Alt+↑]] / [[Alt+↓]] moves it (or the whole selection) up and down; keep pressing to keep moving. Inside the column editor the same keys jump to the previous / next column.
tip.dblclick: Double-click empty canvas for a table, a table name or a column to rename it, a line to edit it, a section title to rename it, a sticky note to type in it.
tip.tab: While naming a column, [[Tab]] saves it and starts the next one; [[Tab]] on the last row adds a new column.
tip.selection: Right-click a selection for “Export selection…”: only the chosen tables, a whole section or a sticky note go into the image or file.
tip.dots: The round dots on a row's edge draw relationships; the + dots on a row's border insert a column there.
tip.color: Header colors and section colors come from one palette; add your own colors and they are saved in the file.
tip.undo: [[Ctrl+Z]] / [[Ctrl+Y]] (or [[Ctrl+Shift+Z]]) undo and redo every change, including drags and resizes; one drag is one step.
tip.persian: The interface can be switched between Persian and English at the top right. Names, types and numbers inside the diagram always stay Latin.
